items.title: Damon Wayans To Guest Star On NBC’s ‘St. Denis Medical’ Season 3 Premiere In ‘In Living Color’ Reunion; First-Look Photo
items.summary: Damon Wayans will guest star on the Season 3 premiere of NBC's "St. Denis Medical," reuniting him with "In Living Color" castmate David Alan Grier. Wayans plays Dr. Highland, a charming but pompous doctor filling in while Grier's Ron recovers from surgery, and everyone at the hospital except Alex is smitten. Deadline reported the casting alongside a first-look photo. Created by Justin Spitzer and Eric Ledgin, the workplace comedy is set at an underfunded Oregon hospital and stars Wendi McLendon-Covey, Allison Tolman, Josh Lawson, Kahyun Kim, Mekki Leeper and Kaliko Kauahi. Season 3, which follows romantic entanglements and personal struggles in the Emergency Department, premieres Monday, November 2 at 8 p.m. on NBC; the first two seasons stream on Peacock. Ledgin is showrunner; Universal Television is the studio.

items.title: Jerry Katzman, Former William Morris President, Dies at 89
items.summary: Jerry Katzman, the TV packaging pioneer who was president of William Morris in the 1990s, died Sunday at his Los Angeles home of Parkinson's disease at 89, per a family spokesperson via The Hollywood Reporter. He joined WMA in 1972, rose from business affairs to head of worldwide television, and assembled elements of series including "The Cosby Show," "Roseanne," "Murphy Brown," "Murder, She Wrote" and "The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air." Clients included Burt Reynolds, Angela Lansbury and Shelley Long. Named president in 1991, vice chairman in 1997, he left in 2002 for UCLA's Producers Program faculty and consulting work with Anonymous Content, and led the Hollywood Radio & Television Society. Born in LA on April 21, 1937, to producer Sam Katzman and actress Hortense Petra, he attended Beverly Hills High, UC Berkeley and UCLA Law. He is survived by wife Carol of 66 years, three children, seven grandchildren and a great-granddaughter.

items.title: Mariska Hargitay’s Best ‘Law & Order: SVU’ Episodes To Re-Air On NBC
items.summary: NBC will air a marathon of Mariska Hargitay's best "Law & Order: SVU" episodes ahead of her Emmys hosting debut: "Charisma" at 8 p.m., the Emmy-winning "911" at 9 p.m., and "Undercover" at 10 p.m. Deadline reported the lineup along with the Season 28 premiere and Hargitay's Emmy stats — a 2006 win for Outstanding Lead Actress and eight nominations for playing Olivia Benson, plus two nods this year as producer and director of the documentary "My Mom Jayne" about Jayne Mansfield. She hosts from the Peacock Theater. The series, executive produced by Dick Wolf and Hargitay among others, also stars Ice-T, Kelli Giddish, Peter Scanavino, Kevin Kane and Aimé Donna Kelly, and will pass 600 episodes later this year.

items.title: Outside Lands 2026 Photo Gallery: The Strokes, Turnstile, Geese, Lucy Dacus, and More
items.summary: Outside Lands 2026 has wrapped at Golden Gate Park in San Francisco, with sets from The Strokes, Turnstile, Geese and Lucy Dacus among the weekend's performances. Consequence published a gallery from photographer Raymond Ahner, who shot the festival on the ground.

items.title: Fuerza Regida Announces New “This Is Our Dream” US Tour Dates
items.summary: Fuerza Regida have added ten dates to their 2026 "This Is Our Dream" Tour, a second leg running through amphitheaters and arenas this fall. The run opens October 3 at Credit Union 1 Amphitheatre in Tinley Park, Illinois, with stops in Charlotte, Atlanta, Birmingham, Albuquerque, Wheatland, Bakersfield, Fresno and West Valley City before closing November 2 at Red Rocks Amphitheatre in Morrison, Colorado. Consequence reported the schedule and ticketing details: a Verizon pre-sale Tuesday, August 11 at 10 a.m. local time, Spotify and Citi cardmember pre-sales at noon, an artist pre-sale August 12, and the general on-sale Friday, August 14 at 10 a.m. local through Ticketmaster. VIP packages for select dates include premium tickets, group photos with select members, lounge access and gift items. The dates follow a sold-out stadium run this year that included Dodger Stadium and Citi Field, and support the album "111XPANTIA," nominated for Best Regional Mexican Music Album at the Grammys.

items.title: Rufus Wainwright, Kathleen Hanna, Yo La Tengo Celebrate the Radical Music of Yoko Ono
items.summary: A 19-song tribute concert, "Yoko Only: A Night Celebrating the Music of Yoko Ono," was staged outside the Broad museum in Los Angeles, tied to the museum's exhibition "Yoko Ono: Music of the Mind." Yo La Tengo served as house band, expanded to five with Nels Cline and Cibo Matto's Yuka Honda, who curated the event and played keyboards. Ono, 93, did not attend. Rolling Stone reported the details. The setlist spanned the avant-garde "AOS" (sung by Theo Bleckmann) to "Walking on Thin Ice" and the post-murder "No, No, No." Performers included Merrill Garbus, Satomi Matsuzaki, Kathleen Hanna with Corin Tucker, Sylvan Esso's Amelia Meath, Finom, Rufus Wainwright and Ono's granddaughter Emi Helfrich. "Yoko Ono was just so ahead of her time and so influential to my generation, the riot grrrl generation," Tucker said backstage. Ira Kaplan joked from the stage about no longer bearing the Beatles a grudge.

items.title: Ariana Grande Charts All 12 Songs From ‘petal’ on Hot 100, Surpasses 100 Career Entries
items.summary: Ariana Grande's new album "petal," released July 31 via Republic, debuts at No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with 295,000 equivalent album units, her seventh chart-topper and first since 2024's "Eternal Sunshine." All 12 tracks land on the Hot 100 dated August 15, led by "Hate That I Made You Love Me" rebounding to No. 2 and the title track debuting at No. 4 — her 24th top 10. Billboard reported the 11 debuts push her career Hot 100 total from 99 to 110, making her the 23rd artist and fourth woman to reach 100 entries, after Taylor Swift, Nicki Minaj and Beyoncé. It's the first time she has charted an entire album inside the Hot 100's top 40. She also returns to No. 1 on the Billboard Artist 100 for an 18th week.

items.title: ‘The Last House’ Star Wagner Moura Talks the Netflix Chart-Topper and Why He Believes the Tide Is Turning for Latino Actors
items.summary: Wagner Moura stars in Louis Leterrier's "The Last House," currently topping Netflix's charts, as engineer Jason Delgado, whose home is sealed shut by an unknown force while he and wife Ann (Greta Lee) try to protect their children. It is Moura's sixth Netflix project since "Narcos," alongside "Sergio," "The Gray Man" and directing on "Narcos: Mexico." Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter, Moura credited both his refusal of typecasting and industry change for his range since 2016: "I think the world is evolving, and it's inevitable that Hollywood will stop seeing a Latino as the violent dude or a Latina as the sexy Latina." He also recounted learning he won the Cannes best actor prize for "The Secret Agent" while shooting close-ups of his hand picking up dog excrement with a third unit. Upcoming projects include the Margot Robbie and Bradley Cooper "Ocean's" prequel and Panos Cosmatos' follow-up to "Mandy."
